title: How Intuit uses LLMs to explain taxes to millions of taxpayers - Jaspreet Singh, Intuit
talk_summary: Intuit's GenOS platform layers prompt-based static and dynamic tax Q&A over a proprietary tax engine, with Claude and GPT models behind an orchestrator that routes queries to the right solution. The most transferable content is their evaluation discipline: tax analysts act as prompt engineers, manual evals seed an LLM-as-judge golden set, and model upgrades are gated on evals.

takeaways.technique: Domain experts as prompt engineers, then LLM-as-judge
takeaways.what_they_do: Tax analysts write the prompts and do initial manual evaluations; their judgments become the golden dataset that trains an LLM-as-judge prompt for automated regression evals on prompt tweaks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: using the tax analysts as the prompt engineers ... get the initial evaluations done that then becomes the basis for automated evaluations

takeaways.what_they_do: Manual expert evals at project start and on major changes (new tax year, big prompt rewrites); cheap automated LLM-judge evals for minor prompt iterations so dev velocity isn't blocked.

takeaways.technique: Static vs dynamic query split across models
takeaways.what_they_do: Prepared-statement-style static queries go to one model (Claude), open-ended dynamic Q&A to another (GPT-4 mini), with a planner classifying incoming queries to pick the solution.
takeaways.evidence_quote: static prompt. Think of it like a prepared statement ... dynamic query would be user have questions

takeaways.what_they_do: Fine-tuned Claude 3 Haiku on static queries so fewer instructions are needed, cutting prompt size and latency while holding quality; found it too specialized for broad use.
takeaways.evidence_quote: biggest driver of course is uh fewer instructions are needed once you have fine-tuned the model ... squeeze down the prompt size

takeaways.technique: Deterministic engine for numbers, LLM only for prose
takeaways.what_they_do: All numeric tax values come from the proprietary tax engine, never the LLM; guardrail ML models check the LLM output for hallucinated numbers before showing users.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We are not having LLMs do the calculations at all ... make sure we did not hallucinate any numbers

takeaways.technique: Graph RAG over plain RAG, plus personalization
takeaways.what_they_do: Use graph-based retrieval over proprietary structured knowledge; reports graph RAG beats regular RAG, and personalization beats both.
takeaways.evidence_quote: graph rack we've definitely seen better response ... even more than that ... personalizing the answers
